# probprog

Probabilistic programming, NumPyro style: programs written with `sample` and `observe`, effect handlers (including `reparam`, `collapse`, `lift`, `scope` and Gen-style trace operations), log densities, model analysis, inference engines (MCMC, variational, SMC, exact enumeration) and a planner that can choose among them (one way in, not the only one), posteriors, predictive distributions and model criticism. The engines folder is part of this entry point. Beside the programs, `model` is the model layer (a builder producing a JSON-able spec with named dimensions, data binding, static analysis, structure reports and drawing, compiled to programs and to factor graphs), `inference` holds the inference methods (each with its own knobs, typed tape, budget and anytime snapshots, and no universal entry point), `models` the benchmark models with their truth, and `validation` the grid oracles, agreement tables, simulation-based calibration and the campaigns that check the engines.

## probprog/engines

The inference engines, part of `omai-engine/probprog`: exact ones (enumeration, conjugate updates, linear-Gaussian conditioning, chain forward-backward), MCMC (NUTS, Gibbs), weighting (importance sampling, SMC, ABC) and approximations (SVI, Laplace, EM), each with the contract that lets the planner choose between them.

## probprog/ep

What a user of expectation propagation on a model needs, and the suite that tests it. The capability: `runEp` runs EP on a bound model through the route that applies (`epRoute` of `probprog/inference`) and returns the beliefs per sweep, a message record and the evidence, or the library's refusal; the check of beliefs against a reference (`atomCheck`), the credible intervals, the calibration and recovery of a method over simulated data sets, the measurement of what EP and the variational method run on (`epCoverage`, `vmpCoverage`) and the registry of gaps and directions. The suite: the atoms (bare setups of one factor or one family each, with a reference answer and a tolerance, in `_atoms/`, one file per family with the basic and learned twins together; the registry `epAtoms` and `epAtom(name)` are the only way to reach one), whose references are in `probprog/validation`. The rules are in `message-passing` and the compiler mappings in `probprog/model`; this folder composes them and nothing in the engine imports it. The design is `docs/probprog/ep.md`.

## probprog/inference

The shared convention of the inference methods of the probabilistic layer, available as `omai-engine/probprog/inference`: what every method has in common (knobs as a `Space`, a typed tape contract, a steppable and resumable algorithm, a capability check, a user-selected budget and anytime snapshots) and nothing that chooses a method for the user (except `epRoute`, which says how expectation propagation runs a model: plain, inside a grid, or not). Each method is its own thing with its own knobs and tape. The folder holds the convention (`method.ts`, `runAnytime`), the methods themselves, one per engine and each beside the engine it wraps (`nutsMethod` with one iteration of every chain per step, `sviMethod`, `gibbsMethod`, `laplaceMethod`, `temperedSmcMethod`, `particleFilterMethod`, `emMethod`, `importanceMethod`, `abcSmcMethod`, the kernels of the sampling library as methods (`rwmMethod`, `malaMethod`, `barkerMethod`, `hmcMethod`, `sliceMethod`, `ellipticalSliceMethod`, `sgldMethod`, `sghmcMethod`, `mclmcMethod`, the ensemble samplers `aiesMethod` and `ensembleSliceMethod`, `cheesMethod`, parallel tempering `temperingMethod`) on a shared driver, the user's plan of blocks with a kernel each run as one sampler (`hybridMethod`), message passing on the factor graph of a spec (`epSpecMethod`, `vmpSpecMethod`, `bpSpecMethod`), and the one-step exact ones), each made from a bound spec or a program, and the model registry by name that lets a worker run one. It also holds the building blocks for methods written on the program layer: kernels defined in a few lines on the handlers and trace operations (`defineKernel`, with a resimulation and a random-walk kernel as worked examples).

## probprog/model

The model layer: a model written once as a value. A builder (`defineModel`) with named dimensions, data, latent, observed, derived, generated and factor nodes, recurrences (`scan`: time series, state-space models, hidden Markov chains) and constraints produces a JSON-able `ModelSpec`; the spec is bound to data (`bind`, `withData`, `bindDataset`), compiled to the existing `sample`/`observe` program (`toProgram`) so every present engine and handler runs it, compiled to a factor graph for message passing with its plates expanded (`toFactorGraph`, with the reasons for what cannot be mapped), analysed without running (`analyseSpec`: dependencies, plates, conjugate pairs), drawn (`toStructure`), composed (`include`, `conditionSpec`, `doSpec`) and serialised (`fromJSON`). Expressions use a closed registry of operators; distributions are named families with the library's constructors behind them (`omai-engine/probprog/model/dists`).

### probprog/model/dists

The distribution constructors of the model layer, available as `omai-engine/probprog/model/dists`: `normal(0, 5)`, `bernoulli({ probs })`, `gamma(2, 1)` and the other families, taking numbers or model expressions and returning a distribution as data, with the table that maps each family name to the library's constructor.

- function `builders.ts` (file): normal, gamma, bernoulli and the other families as model expressions. `src/lib/probprog/model/dists/builders.ts:1` `omai-engine/probprog/model/dists`

- table `families.ts` (file): The distribution families a model spec names, mapped to the library's constructors. `src/lib/probprog/model/dists/families.ts:1` `omai-engine/probprog/model/dists`

### probprog/model/factor-graph

The pieces of the model-to-factor-graph compiler (`toFactorGraph`, in `../factors.ts`) that stand on their own. Public: the types a compilation reports (issues, site layouts, the compilation record), the reading back of a run (`factorGraphPosterior`, `graphOnSpec`) and the verdict for a message-passing method (`factorGraphVerdict`, `operatorsWithout`, `compileFactorGraph`). Private (`_` files and folders, not exported): the refusal the mappings throw, the value algebra they compute with (cells: affine forms over the graph's random scalars, lookups, scaled and reciprocal gamma variables), the graph builder (variables, factors, auxiliary names, atoms), the constants pass, the recognisers of idioms, the layout plan, the context (the state of one compilation), the evaluator of expressions (`_symbolic/`) and the mappings of nodes (`_mappings/`). Re-exported flat into `omai-engine/probprog/model`.

- function `factorGraphPosterior`: The Posterior of a message-passing state, by site name, in the spec's shapes. `src/lib/probprog/model/factor-graph/readback.ts:74` `omai-engine/probprog/model`

## probprog/models

The benchmark models of probabilistic programming, available as `omai-engine/probprog/models`: named models written with `defineModel` (recurrences as `scan` nodes), each with a title, description, tags and references, a seeded data generator beside its canonical data, the truth the inference methods are compared with (a closed form, a quadrature or an analytic marginal) and the plans of the methods that apply to it, with what to expect of each. `benchmarkModels` lists them, `benchmarkEntries` and `benchmarkMethods` hand them to a worker's registry, and `benchmarkCampaigns` is their cross-engine agreement as periodic validation campaigns. The suite so far: the conjugate trio, logistic, probit, Poisson and negative binomial regression, eight schools (centred and non-centred), the Gaussian mixture (with and without label switching), Neal's funnel (centred and non-centred), the banana, a two-mode target, a radon hierarchy, a three-player TrueSkill, an AR(1) state space, and (`additionalBenchmarkModels`) stochastic volatility, a Gaussian HMM, Gaussian process regression (centred and non-centred), a small topic model, a small Bayesian neural network, item response scoring, a stick-breaking mixture and Minka's clutter problem. `kernelCampaigns` is the periodic validation of the kernel methods: Geweke tests, calibration, agreement with the truth of three of them and parallel tempering on the two-mode target.

## probprog/validation

The validation kernel for probabilistic programs: oracles (the grid posterior, closed-form conjugate posteriors), the agreement table that compares posterior approximations with an oracle or each other, simulation-based calibration with the exact rank distribution, Geweke joint-distribution tests, and the runner that gathers campaigns into a report. The library only returns numbers and records; the test helpers that assert on them are in `src/testing`, and the heavy campaigns are a script run on request, not part of the gate.

- function `agree`: Compare posterior approximations with an oracle or each other: moments, KS, Wasserstein, KL. `src/lib/probprog/validation/agree.ts:188` `omai-engine/probprog/validation`
- function `gewekeTest`: Geweke joint-distribution test of a posterior transition operator. `src/lib/probprog/validation/geweke.ts:83` `omai-engine/probprog/validation`
- function `gridPosterior`: Grid posterior of a small program: evidence, marginals and moments to quadrature accuracy. `src/lib/probprog/validation/grid.ts:175` `omai-engine/probprog/validation`
- function `mixtureOfRegressions`: Exact mixture-of-regressions posterior by enumerating the assignments of rows to classes. `src/lib/probprog/validation/enumeration.ts:390` `omai-engine/probprog/validation`
- function `sbc`: Simulation-based calibration of an inference method with the exact rank distribution. `src/lib/probprog/validation/sbc.ts:180` `omai-engine/probprog/validation`
- function `spikeSlabRegression`: Exact spike and slab regression posterior by enumerating the 2^p subsets of coefficients. `src/lib/probprog/validation/enumeration.ts:79` `omai-engine/probprog/validation`
- function `zeroInflatedPoisson`: Exact zero-inflated Poisson regression posterior on a refined grid, structural zeros summed out. `src/lib/probprog/validation/enumeration.ts:250` `omai-engine/probprog/validation`

- estimator `sbcMethod`: Simulation-based calibration, one replication per step, with the tests of the ranks so far. `src/lib/probprog/validation/sbc-method.ts:68` `omai-engine/probprog/validation`

### probprog/validation/references

The reference answers the expectation-propagation atoms are checked against, one family of kernels: the shape of a reference marginal (`ExactMarginal`) and the closed forms that make one, the marginal of a density on a grid (one dimension, a hyperparameter on a log grid, a tensor grid of any dimension, three coordinates found by passes), the exact switches and clutter problems, and the Gibbs sampler of a mixture. Each takes a log density or a model's closed form as a callback, so the reference is written by hand, independent of the rule under test.

- function `clutterPosterior`: Exact clutter posterior with unknown centre, precisions and weight, by quadrature. `src/lib/probprog/validation/references/clutter.ts:51` `omai-engine/probprog/validation`
- function `mixtureGibbs`: Gibbs sampler for a Gaussian mixture, the gate atoms' reference. `src/lib/probprog/validation/references/sampler.ts:79` `omai-engine/probprog/validation`
- function `outlierMixturePosterior`: Exact outlier-mixture posterior with unknown centre, precision and share. `src/lib/probprog/validation/references/clutter.ts:179` `omai-engine/probprog/validation`
